anchor.quote: Let $n$ be the bit length of each input.
Let $b$ be the number of bits in one radix digit
let $q = \lceil n/b \rceil$ be the number of digits in each input
The radix is $Q_0 = 2^b$, the base in which each digit is written.
The index $j$ runs over the positions of the coefficient list, from $0$ upward.
The digit $d_j$ is the $j$th base-$Q_0$ digit of the output
The carry $k_j$ is the amount carried into position $j$ from the lower positions.
$\sum_{h<j} c_h Q_0^h = \sum_{h<j} d_h Q_0^h + k_j Q_0^j.$
anchor.note: h is a summation index in the sum over h<j; the page never says what h denotes or what range it takes beyond the bound h<j.

anchor.quote: where $x \bmod Q_0$ is the remainder of $x$ on division by $Q_0$

gaps.quote: Each product coefficient obeys $0 \le c_j \le q(Q_0-1)^2 < Q_0^3$.
gaps.note: The lower bound and q(Q_0-1)^2 follow from the convolution, but the final inequality q(Q_0-1)^2 < Q_0^3 needs q to be small relative to Q_0, and the page never states or derives that condition on q, n and b.

gaps.quote: the leftover carry is written out the same way, one digit at a time, until it is zero
gaps.note: The page asserts that the leftover carry reaches zero and that every remaining c_h and carry is zero, without showing that the carry eventually vanishes, which requires the reader to see that the carry shrinks once the coefficients are exhausted.
